summary: Draw many copies of one geometry through instance matrices, and keep those matrices from pretending each copy is a simulated body.
objective: Moving one instance via setMatrixAt moves only that copy after needsUpdate; disposing the InstancedMesh frees its GPU buffers.
applies_when: Trees, crates, cobbles, bolts or other repeated props share geometry and material.
Draw-call cost of one mesh per prop is the problem, not per-instance physics.
intent_signals: crate stack that is just copies
example_prompts: Scatter a hundred identical lanterns with InstancedMesh and let me recolour one instance.
Use instancing for cobbles, not a physics body per stone.
negative_signals: One InstancedMesh whose instance matrices are also written by a rigid-body island without a documented copy step.
Claiming instancing simulates contact among instances.
not_for: Unique articulated heroes that need their own skeleton.
Per-instance materials that actually differ in shader feature set rather than a colour tint.

principles: Instancing is a draw technique for many objects that share geometry and material but not world transforms. It is not a particle solver.
Each instance's pose lives in instanceMatrix. The parent Object3D transform still moves the whole batch.
If a subset of instances must collide, give those copies real bodies and treat instancing as presentation, or accept that the batch has no contacts.
implementation: Create InstancedMesh(geometry, material, count). Write poses with setMatrixAt and tints with setColorAt. Set instanceMatrix.needsUpdate (and instanceColor.needsUpdate) after edits.
Keep an application array of instance ids to semantic props. Raycast hits expose instanceId; map that back to the prop, not to a fake body.
Recompute bounding sphere after large pose edits if picking or culling misses instances.
Call dispose when replacing the batch. Reset restores authored matrices, not leftover simulation.
observable_checks: setMatrixAt on one index, with needsUpdate, moves only that instance; neighbours stay put.
setColorAt changes that instance's tint without cloning a material.
A physics debug overlay, if present, does not show a collider per decorative instance unless one was actually created.

creative_affordances: Colour, scale and slight rotation variation among instances is a free art direction.
A few unique hero meshes can sit beside an instanced crowd of the same prop.
known_limits: InstancedMesh requires shared geometry and material(s); it does not create rigid bodies or establish scientific packing.
Authored reusable guidance; no runtime artifact has been observed for this record.

claims.statement: InstancedMesh is a mesh with instanced rendering for a large number of objects that share geometry and material(s) but have different world transformations; setMatrixAt writes a local transform that is uploaded when instanceMatrix.needsUpdate is set true, and dispose frees the GPU resources of that instance.
claims.scope: Three.js InstancedMesh API; instancing is a rendering batch, not a contact model.

source_refs.locator: Opening description; setMatrixAt and instanceMatrix.needsUpdate; dispose
